title: data-visualization Skill Review: Good Chart Rules, Two Different Colour-Blind Palettes
description: We made four charts of our registry with Anthropic's data-visualization skill. They came out clear, labelled and correct. Its colour advice contradicts itself, and it says nothing about sparse dates.

author.name: TrustedSkills Team
author.bio: We assess AI agent skills by installing them, running them against real work, and reading the source. We don't accept payment for reviews.

basisNote: Part of a batch of thirteen data and automation skills run on the same day against the same dataset: this site's own registry index, 26,001 skills in one 71 MB JSON file. Each run worked in its own private copy of the site's repository. One run on one dataset is one data point, not a benchmark.

runs.task: Make four charts for a "state of the registry" page: skills per category, install-status share, verification-tier counts, and skills first published per month. Save them with the script that made them, check each chart's numbers against an independent count, and check the charts against the skill's own design and accessibility guidance.
runs.outcome:
`npx skills add anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins --skill data-visualization` installed it first time.

The agent followed the chart selection guide: sorted horizontal bars for categories and install status, bars for tiers, and a line for the monthly count. Each chart got a headline title that states the finding, a source line, value labels and a separate alt-text file. We looked at the charts: they are clean and readable. Every number matched an independent count in Node.

The skill's colour advice gives two answers. Under "Colorblind-friendly palettes" it hard-codes a list that includes a red and a green, and later it says to use seaborn's `colorblind` palette. Its rule to "grey everything else" was first applied with a second colour; the agent caught it on review and switched to real grey.

The data had a trap. Only 101 of 26,001 skills have a publish date. The skill has no advice on sparse or missing time data, so the agent decided to fill empty months with zero and made the gap the chart's headline.
runs.environment: Claude Code subagent (Sonnet 5) with the installed SKILL.md loaded as its instructions, in a private clone of the TrustedSkills website repo at commit 5169470. Python virtualenv with matplotlib and seaborn.

summary: A solid chart guide in one file: how to pick a chart, ready-made matplotlib code, and a design and accessibility checklist. Our four charts came out clear and correct. Pick one palette yourself, because the skill offers two that disagree. Check date coverage before you draw a trend line, because the skill will not.

strengths.title: Chart choice by data relationship
strengths.body: A short guide maps comparison, share, distribution and trend to chart types, with a list of charts to avoid.

strengths.title: Accessibility checklist you can run
strengths.body: Alt text, direct labels, no colour-only meaning. Our run produced alt text for every chart because the checklist asked for it.

strengths.title: Titles that state the finding
strengths.body: The design section pushes titles like "71% of skills install cleanly" instead of "Install status".

limitations.title: Contradictory colour-blind advice
limitations.body: The hard-coded "colorblind-friendly" list contains red and green, against the skill's own "avoid red/green" rule. A later line points to a different palette.

limitations.title: Nothing on sparse or missing dates
limitations.body: It does not warn that a time series with gaps can mislead, or say how to fill them.

limitations.title: Not recently maintained
limitations.body: The skill's folder was last changed in March 2026.

bestFor.title: Report and dashboard charts in Python
bestFor.body: Choose seaborn's colorblind palette and check field coverage before you plot.

notFor: Interactive web charts in JavaScript. The code patterns are matplotlib, seaborn and a little Plotly in Python.
